8. PREVIOUSMONTH, PREVIOUSQUARTER, PREVIOUSYEAR 🟡

📘 Definition: PREVIOUSMONTH, PREVIOUSQUARTER, and PREVIOUSYEAR are DAX Time Intelligence functions that return the complete set of dates for the previous month, quarter, or year respectively — relative to the last date in the current filter context. Unlike DATEADD, these functions always return the full previous period, not a partial shift.

🎯 Samjho Hinglish Mein: DATEADD flexible hai — kitne bhi period shift karo. PREVIOUSMONTH, PREVIOUSQUARTER, PREVIOUSYEAR simple aur direct hain — sirf ek period peeche jaate hain aur poora period cover karte hain. June 2023 ke liye PREVIOUSMONTH = poora May 2023. Q2 ke liye PREVIOUSQUARTER = poora Q1. 2023 ke liye PREVIOUSYEAR = poora 2022. Quick comparison ke liye perfect!

💡 Syntax:

PREVIOUSMONTH(dates) PREVIOUSQUARTER(dates) PREVIOUSYEAR(dates, [year_end_date]) -- dates = DateTable[Date] column -- Always CALCULATE ke andar use karo

💻 DAX Examples:

-- Example 1: Previous Month Sales Sales PM = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), PREVIOUSMONTH(DateTable[Date]) ) -- June 2023 filter → poora May 2023 ka total -- Example 2: Previous Quarter Sales Sales PQ = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), PREVIOUSQUARTER(DateTable[Date]) ) -- Q2 (Apr-Jun) → Q1 (Jan-Mar) ka total -- Example 3: Previous Year Sales Sales PY = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), PREVIOUSYEAR(DateTable[Date]) ) -- 2023 → poora 2022 ka total -- Example 4: QoQ Growth % QoQ Growth % = DIVIDE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]) - CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), PREVIOUSQUARTER(DateTable[Date]) ), CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), PREVIOUSQUARTER(DateTable[Date]) ), 0 ) -- Q2 vs Q1 growth percentage

📊 Expected Output:

Period Current Sales Previous Month Previous Quarter Previous Year
March 202318,00012,000—16,000
Q2 20231,37,000—1,15,000—
2023 Total4,19,500——3,80,000
📋 DATEADD vs PREVIOUS functions:
• ✅ PREVIOUSMONTH = DATEADD(-1, MONTH) — same result, simpler syntax
• ✅ PREVIOUSQUARTER = DATEADD(-1, QUARTER)
• ✅ PREVIOUSYEAR = DATEADD(-1, YEAR)
• 💡 PREVIOUS functions more readable hain — beginners ke liye better
• 💡 DATEADD use karo jab -2, -3 ya custom intervals chahiye

⚠️ Common Mistakes

⚠️ Date Table Mistakes:
  • Date Table nahi banai — Time Intelligence functions BLANK return karte hain. Fix: CALENDAR ya CALENDARAUTO se Date Table banao aur Mark as Date Table karo
  • Date column mein gaps hain — YTD, QTD calculations galat aate hain. Fix: CALENDAR use karo continuous dates ke liye
  • Relationship nahi banaya — Sales Table aur Date Table ka connection missing. Fix: Model View mein Order Date se Date column ka relationship banao
  • Date column text format mein hai — DAX functions date recognize nahi karte. Fix: Power Query mein data type Date set karo
⚠️ DAX Formula Mistakes:
  • TOTALYTD mein Sales column use kiya DateTable ki jagah — Wrong dates column. Fix: hamesha DateTable[Date] use karo
  • SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR bina CALCULATE ke use kiya — Error aayega. Fix: hamesha CALCULATE ke andar wrap karo
  • DIVIDE ki jagah direct division / — Zero error aata hai. Fix: DIVIDE(numerator, denominator, 0) use karo
  • Fiscal year end date galat likhi — "31-03" ki jagah "03-31" likhna hai. Fix: format "MM-DD" hota hai, "DD-MM" nahi

💬 Interview Questions

Q1: Power BI mein Date Table kyu zaroori hai?
Ans: Date Table Power BI mein Time Intelligence functions ka foundation hai. Bina proper Date Table ke TOTALYTD, SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR, DATEADD jaise functions correctly kaam nahi karte. Sales Table mein sirf woh dates hoti hain jab transactions hue — kuch dates missing ho sakti hain. Date Table mein 1 Jan se 31 Dec tak har ek date hoti hai — no gaps. Yeh continuity Time Intelligence ke liye mandatory hai. Date Table ko Mark as Date Table karna padta hai aur Sales Table se relationship banana padta hai Order Date ke through.

Q2: CALENDAR aur CALENDARAUTO mein kya difference hai?
Ans: CALENDAR mein aap manually start aur end date specify karte ho — DATE(2023,1,1) se DATE(2023,12,31) tak. CALENDARAUTO automatically aapke poore data model mein sab date columns scan karta hai, minimum aur maximum date detect karta hai, aur usi range ki Date Table bana deta hai. CALENDARAUTO zyada smart hai — data update hone par automatically adjust bhi ho jaata hai. CALENDAR tab use karo jab exact date range control chahiye, CALENDARAUTO tab jab automation chahiye.

Q3: TOTALYTD aur DATESYTD mein kya antar hai?
Ans: TOTALYTD ek shortcut function hai jo internally CALCULATE aur DATESYTD dono ko combine karta hai — directly expression aur dates dete hain. DATESYTD sirf dates ka set return karta hai — isko CALCULATE ke andar manually use karna padta hai. Example: TOTALYTD(SUM(Sales[Amount]), DateTable[Date]) = CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Amount]), DATESYTD(DateTable[Date])). TOTALYTD simpler aur quick hai, DATESYTD zyada flexible hai jab additional filters bhi add karne ho CALCULATE mein.

Q4: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR aur DATEADD(-1, YEAR) mein kya difference hai?
Ans: Dono functions same result dete hain majority cases mein — exactly 1 year peeche shift karte hain. Difference leap year pe aata hai — 29 February wale saal mein SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR thoda differently handle karta hai. DATEADD zyada flexible hai kyunki aap koi bhi number of intervals specify kar sakte ho — -2 YEAR, -3 MONTH, etc. SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR sirf 1 year peeche jaata hai. Readability ke liye SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR zyada clear hai — naam se hi pata chalta hai kya kar raha hai.

Q5: Indian Fiscal Year (April-March) ke liye TOTALYTD kaise use karenge?
Ans: TOTALYTD mein ek optional 4th argument hota hai — year_end_date. Indian fiscal year March 31 pe khatam hota hai. Isliye formula hoga: TOTALYTD(SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), DateTable[Date], "03-31"). Yahaan "03-31" matlab March 31 — format MM-DD hota hai. Isse April 1 se March 31 tak ka cumulative total milega — Indian government aur corporate reporting ke liye standard. Agar yeh argument na likho toh default December 31 use hoga jo calendar year hota hai.

Q6: PREVIOUSMONTH aur DATEADD(-1, MONTH) — kaunsa use karna chahiye?
Ans: Dono same result dete hain — previous complete month ki dates. Choice preference aur readability pe based hai. PREVIOUSMONTH ka naam self-explanatory hai — code padne wale ko turant samajh aata hai. DATEADD(-1, MONTH) zyada flexible hai — -2, -3 months bhi easily change kar sakte ho. Best practice: sirf ek period peeche ke liye PREVIOUSMONTH use karo — cleaner aur readable. Multiple periods peeche ke liye DATEADD use karo. Interview mein dono batao aur yeh difference explain karo — shows deep knowledge.

Q7: Time Intelligence functions kab BLANK return karte hain?
Ans: Time Intelligence functions BLANK return karte hain jab: (1) Date Table nahi bani ya Mark as Date Table nahi kiya — engine samajhta nahi kaunsi Date Table use karni hai. (2) Date Table aur Sales Table ke beech relationship missing hai. (3) Date column mein data type Date nahi hai — text hai. (4) Selected period se pehle ka data exist nahi karta — example January ke liye PREVIOUSMONTH BLANK dega agar December previous year mein data nahi hai. (5) Date column mein gaps hain — TOTALYTD uneven results deta hai. Fix: proper Date Table, correct relationship, Date data type ensure karo.

Q8: YoY Growth % formula mein DIVIDE kyu use karte hain simple division ki jagah?
Ans: Simple division operator (/) use karne se jab denominator zero hota hai — Power BI error ya infinity show karta hai visual mein jo professional nahi dikhta. DIVIDE function teen arguments leta hai — numerator, denominator, aur alternate_result. Jab denominator zero ho tab DIVIDE automatically alternate_result return karta hai — usually 0 ya BLANK. Example: DIVIDE(CurrentSales - LastYearSales, LastYearSales, 0). Agar last year data nahi tha toh 0 return karega instead of error. YoY, MoM sab growth calculations mein DIVIDE use karna best practice hai — clean, error-free reports milte hain.

1. PARALLELPERIOD — Period Parallel Comparison 🔴

📘 Definition: PARALLELPERIOD is a DAX Time Intelligence function that returns a table of dates representing a period parallel to the dates in the specified dates column, shifted by a number of intervals. Unlike DATEADD which shifts partial periods, PARALLELPERIOD always returns a complete parallel period — the full month, quarter, or year shifted by the specified number of intervals.

🎯 Samjho Hinglish Mein: PARALLELPERIOD aur DATEADD mein ek important difference hai. Maan lo abhi March 15, 2023 hai. DATEADD(-1, MONTH) dega February 15 — sirf wo specific date shifted. PARALLELPERIOD(-1, MONTH) dega poora February 2023 — 1st se 28th tak. PARALLELPERIOD hamesha complete period return karta hai — partial nahi. Quarterly dashboard mein Q2 vs Q1 complete comparison ke liye perfect — poora Q1 return karega, na ki sirf shifted dates.

💡 Syntax:

PARALLELPERIOD(dates, number_of_intervals, interval) -- dates = DateTable[Date] column -- number_of_intervals = + forward, - backward -- interval = MONTH, QUARTER, YEAR -- Always use inside CALCULATE

💻 DAX Examples:

-- Example 1: Previous Complete Month Sales Sales Parallel PM = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), PARALLELPERIOD(DateTable[Date], -1, MONTH) ) -- March 2023 → complete February 2023 total -- Chahe March ka sirf 1 din select ho — poora Feb aayega -- Example 2: Previous Complete Quarter Sales Sales Parallel PQ = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), PARALLELPERIOD(DateTable[Date], -1, QUARTER) ) -- Q2 2023 → complete Q1 2023 (Jan+Feb+Mar) total -- Example 3: Same Quarter Last Year Sales Same Q Last Year = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), PARALLELPERIOD(DateTable[Date], -4, QUARTER) ) -- Q2 2023 → Q2 2022 (4 quarters peeche = 1 saal peeche same quarter) -- Example 4: Previous Complete Year Sales Parallel PY = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), PARALLELPERIOD(DateTable[Date], -1, YEAR) ) -- 2023 → complete 2022 total

📊 PARALLELPERIOD vs DATEADD — Key Difference:

Scenario DATEADD Result PARALLELPERIOD Result
March 15 selected, -1 MONTHFeb 15 onlyFull February (1-28)
Q2 selected, -1 QUARTERShifts each date by 3 monthsFull Q1 (Jan+Feb+Mar)
2023 selected, -1 YEAREach date shifted 1 year backFull 2022 (Jan-Dec)
Best UsePartial period comparisonFull period comparison

2. NEXTMONTH, NEXTQUARTER, NEXTYEAR 🔴

📘 Definition: NEXTMONTH, NEXTQUARTER, and NEXTYEAR are DAX Time Intelligence functions that return a table of all dates from the next month, next quarter, or next year respectively — relative to the last date in the current filter context. These are used for forward-looking analysis such as forecasting, target setting, and pipeline reporting.

🎯 Samjho Hinglish Mein: PREVIOUS functions peeche dekhte hain — NEXT functions aage dekhte hain. June 2023 ke liye NEXTMONTH = July 2023 ka poora data. Q2 ke liye NEXTQUARTER = Q3 (Jul-Sep). Forecast dashboards mein use hota hai — agle mahine ki targets vs actuals, pipeline analysis, aur budget planning. Real-world mein less common hai kyunki future data hota nahi — lekin comparative analysis mein useful hai.

💡 Syntax:

NEXTMONTH(dates) NEXTQUARTER(dates) NEXTYEAR(dates, [year_end_date]) -- dates = DateTable[Date] -- Always inside CALCULATE

💻 DAX Examples:

-- Example 1: Next Month Sales (if data exists) Sales Next Month = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), NEXTMONTH(DateTable[Date]) ) -- January 2023 selected → February 2023 sales -- Future months mein BLANK aayega (data nahi hai) -- Example 2: Next Quarter Sales Sales Next Quarter = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), NEXTQUARTER(DateTable[Date]) ) -- Q1 2023 selected → Q2 2023 (Apr+May+Jun) total -- Example 3: Next Year Sales Sales Next Year = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), NEXTYEAR(DateTable[Date]) ) -- 2022 selected → 2023 ka poora total -- Example 4: Current vs Next Month Comparison MoM Forward % = DIVIDE( CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), NEXTMONTH(DateTable[Date]) ) - SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), 0 ) -- Kitna change hoga next month — forward looking

Q1 20231,15,000—1,37,000 (Q2)
2022 Full Year2,04,500——
⚡ Important Note: NEXT functions future data ke liye BLANK return karte hain agar Data Table mein woh dates hain but Sales mein transactions nahi hain. Forecast dashboards mein inhe budget/target tables ke saath combine karte hain — actual sales table mein future data nahi hoga.

3. CALCULATE + Time Intelligence Combo 🔴

📘 Definition: CALCULATE is the most powerful DAX function that evaluates an expression in a modified filter context. When combined with Time Intelligence functions, CALCULATE acts as the engine that applies the date filter returned by functions like SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR, DATEADD, or PARALLELPERIOD to compute measures for specific time periods.

🎯 Samjho Hinglish Mein: Time Intelligence functions sirf dates ka set return karte hain — calculation nahi karte. CALCULATE us date set ko filter ki tarah use karke actual calculation karta hai. CALCULATE ke bina Time Intelligence functions akele kaam nahi karte. Jaise SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR sirf "last year ki dates do" bolta hai — CALCULATE us filter pe SUM karta hai. CALCULATE = engine, Time Intelligence = fuel.

💻 Advanced CALCULATE Combos:

-- Example 1: CALCULATE with multiple filters North Sales Last Year = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(DateTable[Date]), Sales[Region] = "North" ) -- Last year ki sales sirf North region ki -- Time Intelligence + Region filter dono ek saath -- Example 2: CALCULATE with DATEADD + Product filter Laptop Sales 3M Ago = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), DATEADD(DateTable[Date], -3, MONTH), Sales[Product] = "Laptop" ) -- 3 months pehle sirf Laptop ki sales -- Example 3: Running Total using CALCULATE Running Total = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), FILTER( ALL(DateTable), DateTable[Date] <= MAX(DateTable[Date]) ) ) -- Har row tak cumulative total — TOTALYTD se alag -- Yeh year boundary cross bhi karta hai -- Example 4: CALCULATE with TOTALYTD override YTD North Laptop = CALCULATE( TOTALYTD( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), DateTable[Date] ), Sales[Region] = "North", Sales[Product] = "Laptop" ) -- YTD calculation sirf North region ke Laptop ke liye -- CALCULATE ke andar TOTALYTD — double nesting possible!

Month Total Sales North LY Running Total

February 202312,000BLANK97,000
March 202318,000BLANK1,15,000

4. DATESYTD, DATESQTD, DATESMTD — Filter Versions 🔴

📘 Definition: DATESYTD, DATESQTD, and DATESMTD are DAX functions that return a table of dates from the beginning of the year, quarter, or month up to the last date in the current filter context. Unlike TOTALYTD/TOTALQTD/TOTALMTD which directly calculate, these functions only return date sets and must be used inside CALCULATE — giving more flexibility to add additional filters.

🎯 Samjho Hinglish Mein: TOTALYTD ek shortcut hai — directly result deta hai. DATESYTD sirf dates ka set deta hai — calculation CALCULATE karta hai. Difference yeh hai ki DATESYTD ke saath CALCULATE mein aur bhi filters add kar sakte ho. Jaise YTD sirf North region ki sales chahiye — CALCULATE(SUM(...), DATESYTD(...), Region="North"). TOTALYTD mein yeh flexibility nahi hoti direct way mein.

💡 Syntax:

DATESYTD(dates, [year_end_date]) DATESQTD(dates) DATESMTD(dates) -- dates = DateTable[Date] -- Hamesha CALCULATE ke andar use karo

💻 DAX Examples:

-- Example 1: DATESYTD basic — same as TOTALYTD Sales YTD v2 = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), DATESYTD(DateTable[Date]) ) -- TOTALYTD(SUM(...), DateTable[Date]) ke barabar -- Example 2: DATESYTD with extra Region filter North YTD Sales = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), DATESYTD(DateTable[Date]), Sales[Region] = "North" ) -- YTD but sirf North region — extra filter add kiya -- Example 3: DATESMTD — Month to Date Sales MTD v2 = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), DATESMTD(DateTable[Date]) ) -- Example 4: DATESQTD with Product filter Laptop QTD = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), DATESQTD(DateTable[Date]), Sales[Product] = "Laptop" ) -- Quarter to Date but sirf Laptop product -- Example 5: Fiscal Year DATESYTD Fiscal YTD = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), DATESYTD(DateTable[Date], "03-31") ) -- Indian fiscal year April se March
📋 TOTALYTD vs DATESYTD — Kab kya use karein:
• ✅ Simple YTD calculation → TOTALYTD (shorter, cleaner)
• ✅ YTD + extra filters (Region, Product) → DATESYTD inside CALCULATE
• ✅ Fiscal year → dono mein year_end_date parameter available
• ✅ Complex nested calculations → DATESYTD zyada flexible

5. DATESBETWEEN & DATESINPERIOD — Custom Date Ranges 🔴

📘 Definition: DATESBETWEEN returns all dates between a specified start date and end date (inclusive). DATESINPERIOD returns dates starting from a specified start date and going back or forward by a given number of intervals. Both functions give precise control over custom date ranges — beyond what standard YTD or PREVIOUSMONTH provides.

🎯 Samjho Hinglish Mein: Kabhi kabhi standard functions se kaam nahi chalta. Manager bolta hai "15 March se 30 June tak ki sales dikhao" — koi standard function yeh nahi karta. DATESBETWEEN exact start aur end date do — usi range ki sales milegi. DATESINPERIOD bolta hai "aaj se pichle 90 din ki sales do" — yeh rolling windows ke liye perfect hai. Custom financial periods, project timelines, promotion periods — sab ke liye useful.

💡 Syntax:

DATESBETWEEN(dates, start_date, end_date) DATESINPERIOD(dates, start_date, number_of_intervals, interval) -- DATESBETWEEN: fixed start aur end date -- DATESINPERIOD: start date se kitne intervals cover karne hain -- interval = DAY, MONTH, QUARTER, YEAR

💻 DAX Examples:

-- Example 1: DATESBETWEEN — Fixed Range Sales Sales Q1 Fixed = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), DATESBETWEEN( DateTable[Date], DATE(2023, 1, 1), DATE(2023, 3, 31) ) ) -- 1 Jan 2023 se 31 Mar 2023 tak total = 1,15,000 -- Example 2: DATESBETWEEN — Mid-year Custom Range Sales H2 2023 = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), DATESBETWEEN( DateTable[Date], DATE(2023, 7, 1), DATE(2023, 12, 31) ) ) -- July se December 2023 — second half sales -- Example 3: DATESINPERIOD — Last 3 Months Sales Last 3M = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), DATESINPERIOD( DateTable[Date], MAX(DateTable[Date]), -3, MONTH ) ) -- Current max date se peeche 3 mahine ka total -- Rolling 3 Month window! -- Example 4: DATESINPERIOD — Last 90 Days Sales Last 90 Days = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), DATESINPERIOD( DateTable[Date], MAX(DateTable[Date]), -90, DAY ) ) -- Last 90 days rolling window

6. Rolling 3 / 6 / 12 Month Sales 🔴

📘 Definition: Rolling Period calculations compute the total or average of a measure over a sliding window of time — such as the last 3, 6, or 12 months — that moves forward as time progresses. Unlike fixed YTD which resets every January, rolling calculations always look at the most recent N months regardless of year boundaries.

🎯 Samjho Hinglish Mein: YTD January mein reset ho jaata hai — December mein 12 months ka data, February mein sirf 2 months ka. Rolling Sales yeh problem solve karta hai. Rolling 3 Month = hamesha last 3 mahine ka total — chahe January ho ya November. Trend analysis ke liye perfect — seasonal fluctuations smooth ho jaate hain. E-commerce, FMCG, retail dashboards mein bahut use hota hai.

💻 DAX Examples:

-- Example 1: Rolling 3 Month Sales Rolling 3M Sales = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), DATESINPERIOD( DateTable[Date], MAX(DateTable[Date]), -3, MONTH ) ) -- June 2023 → Apr+May+Jun total -- September 2023 → Jul+Aug+Sep total -- Example 2: Rolling 6 Month Sales Rolling 6M Sales = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), DATESINPERIOD( DateTable[Date], MAX(DateTable[Date]), -6, MONTH ) ) -- June 2023 → Jan+Feb+Mar+Apr+May+Jun total -- Example 3: Rolling 12 Month Sales (Last 1 Year) Rolling 12M Sales = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales Amount]), DATESINPERIOD( DateTable[Date], MAX(DateTable[Date]), -12, MONTH ) ) -- Last 12 months — crosses year boundary too! -- Dec 2023 → Jan 2023 to Dec 2023 -- Example 4: Rolling 3M Average Rolling 3M Avg = CALCULATE( AVERAGE(Sales[Sales Amount]), DATESINPERIOD( DateTable[Date], MAX(DateTable[Date]), -3, MONTH ) ) -- 3 mahine ka average — trend smoothing ke liye
